seo.title: Branding
seo.description: The official Kleeja logos, the brand colours, and where each one may be used.

branding.title: Kleeja branding
branding.intro: These are the official Kleeja logos. Use them to point at Kleeja — on a site that runs it, in an article about it, or in a talk. This page says which file belongs where, and what the marks may not be used for.
branding.creditLine: Kleeja and the Kleeja logo are marks of the Kleeja project, used here with permission.

logos.title: The logos
logos.intro: The mark is a K built from a coral stem and a navy body. There are two versions of it, one for light surfaces and one for dark, and no drawn wordmark — where the name appears beside the mark it is set in ordinary text.
logos.printNote: Kleeja has no Pantone reference. In print, match the coral to #F45B69 and the navy to #0B1F3A rather than substituting a near-enough colour from whatever palette is to hand.

primary.title: Primary logo
primary.description: Navy and coral. For white and other light backgrounds.

reverse.title: Reverse logo
reverse.description: White and coral. For navy, black, photographs and other dark backgrounds.

logos.formatHint: Reach for the SVG wherever the tool will take it — it is the original and stays sharp at any size. The PNG is 1024×1024 on a transparent background, for tools that cannot read SVG.

clearSpace.title: Clear space
clearSpace.description: Keep free space around the mark on all four sides, at least a quarter of its height. Nothing comes inside that margin — no text, no borders, no other logos.

minSize.title: Minimum size
minSize.description: Never below 24 px on screen, or 10 mm in print. Smaller than that, the notch between the stem and the body closes up and the K stops reading.

misuse.title: What not to do
misuse.intro: The logos can’t be manipulated, recoloured or built into a logo of your own. Six things that break the mark:

recolor.title: Don’t recolour it
recolor.description: Coral with navy, or coral with white. No other pairing, and no gradients.

stretch.title: Don’t stretch it
stretch.description: Scale both sides by the same amount and keep the mark square.

rotate.title: Don’t rotate it
rotate.description: It sits upright, at any size, on any background.

effects.title: Don’t add effects
effects.description: No shadows, glows, outlines, bevels or blurs of any kind.

contrast.title: Don’t lose the contrast
contrast.description: The navy mark disappears on a dark surface. Switch to the reverse version instead.

crop.title: Don’t crop or redraw it
crop.description: Use the file as it is. Don’t trace it, round it off, or lock it up with another logo.

website.title: On a site that runs Kleeja
website.description: A site running Kleeja may say so. Put the logo, or a plain “Powered by Kleeja” line, in the footer or on an about page, and link it to kleeja.net. No permission is needed, and nothing in the licence requires it either — it is yours to decide.

poweredBy.title: “Powered by Kleeja” in a footer
poweredBy.description: Drop this into the footer template of your style.

badge.title: A badge for a README
badge.description: Markdown for a plugin, a style, or a project built on Kleeja.

articles.title: Blog posts and articles
articles.description: Anything in the standard asset set can be used in an article, tutorial, review or comparison about Kleeja, alongside screenshots of the upload page and the Admin Panel. Add the credit line once, in a footer or at the end of the piece.

credit.title: The credit line
credit.description: One line, used as it is, wherever a Kleeja mark appears in a piece you publish.

screenshots.title: Screenshots
screenshots.description: Screenshots of a stock installation are welcome anywhere this page allows the logos. Please don’t edit them to show features Kleeja doesn’t have, or to attribute someone else’s interface to Kleeja.

describe.title: Describing Kleeja
describe.intro: Three ready-made descriptions. Copy whichever one fits the space you have instead of writing your own — that is what they are here for.
describe.oneLineText: Kleeja is a free, open-source PHP script for running a file upload service on your own hosting.
describe.shortText: Kleeja is a free, open-source file upload script written in PHP. Install it on your own hosting and any domain — or any folder on it — becomes a complete upload centre with its own users, styles, plugins and Admin Panel.
describe.longText: Kleeja is a free and open-source file upload and sharing application written in PHP, used by thousands of webmasters since 2007 and running on almost any hosting that supports PHP and MySQL. Once installed, it turns a domain or a folder on it into a full upload centre: visitors upload files within the limits you set, while file types, sizes, users, abuse reports and storage are all managed from the Admin Panel. Its look is changed by installing a style and its features extended by installing a plugin, both from a store built into the Admin Panel. The source code is released under the MIT licence at github.com/kleeja/kleeja.

slides.title: Presentation slides
slides.description: The same asset set is fine in a talk, a course or a workshop. The credit line appears once per deck, on or before the first slide that carries a Kleeja mark.

assetSet.title: The standard asset set
assetSet.description: Where the sections above say “the standard asset set”, they mean these files and nothing else. Anything outside the set — a mark you drew yourself, an old logo from a previous release, an icon lifted from a style — is not covered.
assetSet.primary: The primary logo, as SVG or PNG
assetSet.reverse: The reverse logo, as SVG or PNG
assetSet.screenshots: Your own screenshots of a stock Kleeja installation

colors.title: Colours
colors.intro: Coral is the accent and carries the brand; navy is the ink it sits on. Click a value to copy it.

coral.name: Kleeja Coral
coral.role: Primary. Links, buttons, and the stem of the K.

navy.name: Kleeja Navy
navy.role: The body of the K, and headings on light backgrounds.

white.name: White
white.role: Page backgrounds, and the mark on dark surfaces.

colors.note: Coral on white measures 3.2:1, under the 4.5:1 that WCAG AA asks of small text. Keep it for large text, icons and filled areas, and set body copy in navy.

license.title: About the licence
license.description: Kleeja’s source code is released under the MIT licence, so you are free to use, change and redistribute it. That licence covers the code, not the name or the logos: those identify the project, and the guidelines on this page are what keep them meaning one thing. If your case isn’t covered here, ask — the answer is usually yes.
